prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1474; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers were dispatched to a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas, where two vehicles came together nearly nose to nose. Driver 1 was traveling in one direction when the other vehicle, operated by Driver 2, crossed into its lane. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash and was evaluated at the scene. The force of the impact appeared to be sufficient to produce that kind of injury. Damage to both vehicles lined up with the path and force described by the drivers, and the officer saw no signs of older damage on either car. Photographs taken at the scene confirm several of the reported details, although no independent witnesses came forward. Driver 2 and a Passenger who was riding with Driver 1 both confirmed that Driver 1 was inside the vehicle at the time of the crash. Driver 1 was identified as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle, which was verified during the stop. No citations were issued at the scene pending further review of the statements and physical evidence.
